title: A dragon with no pearl tile in view explores towards the map centre in the opening: on Devil we spend 68% of r1-30 in our empty home strip (leader 19%)
hypothesis: I132's direction, narrowed by a condition the bot can see, with Devil evidence. Devil is our worst map online (submission 6111: lost 11 of 21, 7 by elimination). Each side starts in a 6-column strip at its own edge (x 0-5, 26-31) with no pearl tiles; the pearl columns are towards the middle. Share of dragon-turns in r1-30 inside one's own home strip: us 0.68 (21 games), opponents 0.48, leader 55 0.19 (143305). Pearls per dragon-turn: 0.058 vs 0.084 vs 0.139. Pearls eaten in r0-30: 11.0 vs 16.9 vs 30. Mean head distance to the centre at r10/20/30: 13.1 vs 10.1 vs 5.8. Dragons / total length at r50: 10.5 / 28.4 vs 15.5 / 39.4 (leader 22 / 54). Watched: 234394 dragon 9 walked N up x=31 and S down x=30 for r1-22 with nothing in view and first ate at r23; dragons 7 and 11 did the same. Leader 55's six dragons walked W along the open band y 7-9 and were eating by r11. Big Empty shows a milder version: r0-30 eaten 23.6 vs 28.4, distance to centre 37.3 vs 32.5. It's our trait in wins too (home share 0.66 in Devil wins vs 0.70 in losses), so expect a gain in opening mass rather than a flipped result on its own. Cause: targets.hpp Targets::bestStaleTile. Every never-seen tile scores staleCap, so 3*stale - 2*dist + 2*friendDist picks the nearest unseen grid tile away from teammates, which is the empty strip at home. Change, behind its own switch: while w.round < P.openingRounds (new, start 60), and only when no visible tile has w.spawnKind == SPAWN_YES (the dragon sees nothing that can ever spawn a pearl), add P.openingCentreWeight (new, start 2) x (torusDist(head, centre) - torusDist(t, centre)) to each grid tile's score, with centre = (W/2, H/2). Pearl, spawn and farm targets are unchanged; only explore targets move. Scenarios: (1) Devil r3, a length-2 dragon at (31,8), nothing but empty tiles in view: its explore target is west of its head, towards x 16, not north or south along the strip. (2) The same dragon with one spawn tile in view: target unchanged from today. (3) Boundary: the same state at r60: unchanged. (4) A dragon with a pearl target: unchanged (explore isn't consulted). (5) A symmetric map whose home area has pearl tiles in view (Default Small): unchanged. Measure: home-strip share and pearls eaten in r0-30 on near_devil (baselines above), dragons and mass at r50, and wins on near_devil, near_big_empty, near_trophy. Check it costs nothing on stronghold and trauma, where the centre sits behind portals or kelp.

title: Race for the centre in the opening: on small maps, dragons walk to the map's centre before combing home ground
hypothesis: Change, behind a new switch P.openingCentreRush in a new module (e.g. bot/opening.hpp, wired from Targets::update): while round < P.openingRounds (start 30) and the map has W*H <= P.openingMaxArea (start 1024), a dragon whose path distance (DistField over known edges) to the tile nearest ((W-1)/2, (H-1)/2) is at most P.openingCentreMaxDist (start 24) and more than P.openingArriveRadius (start 3) targets that centre tile instead of choosePearl's out-of-sight candidates (remembered, teammate-shared, probable and spawn-countdown pearls). Visible pearls at most P.openingDetour (start 2) steps off its path are still eaten on the way. It ends for good for that dragon once its head is within P.openingArriveRadius of the centre, once the centre tile has been in its 7x7 view, or at P.openingRounds; then normal targeting eats the pile it can now see. Why: a symmetric map's centre is the same path distance from both teams' starts. Ground near home stays ours; ground in the middle goes to whoever comes first. Nobody visits it early, so a pile builds up there: at r20 the centre quarter held 16 of the map's 30 pearls on Devil and 6 of 16 on Trophy. Devil's centre also holds 8 of its 18 gap-(1,1) tiles, including two 2x2 loops where one dragon eats 2 pearls and splits every 5-7 rounds; Trophy's cup holds its only fast tiles (11 at gap 5-30, against 582 tiles at 1-1000). Evidence, online submission 6542 (60 games, 44-16), centre-quarter eats in r0-60 (audit 1790370853305270000, F1): on Devil, Trophy and Default Small, when the opponent out-ate us there we went 1-8 (Devil 245480 7v47, 246198 4v58, 245936 21v40, 245419 26v30; Trophy 245044 0v33, 245420 4v17, 245465 1v27; Default Small 245462 9v22); when we out-ate them we went 10-1. The race: their first centre eat came at r10-28, ours at r16-37 or never; in the only Devil win (246384 vs 839) we arrived at r37, before 839 at r44. Leader 470 took the Default Small centre 20v9 (162467). Watched: 791's dragon 0 in 245480 walked east from its start and ate 9 in 9 rounds (r24-32, length 2 to 11); 473's dragon 2 in Trophy 245044 was eating in the cup at r14; our 245480 dragon 1 spent r1-45 in the x=26 tunnel beside its start. Births per dragon-turn in r0-60 were level (us 0.027-0.049, them 0.034-0.048), so the pile is what the opponents grow from: in 245480 r40-79, from 10v9 dragons, we made 12 births to their 33. Cause: Targets::update runs choosePearl first; from r0 every seen tile gives a countdown or probable candidate within P.maxTargetDist, so exploring rarely runs; when it does, bestStaleTile's -2 per step makes the nearest never-seen tile win. How often: 7 of 16 losses in 6542 are on Devil and Trophy, 10 of 16 on Devil, Trophy, Default Small and Default. Scenarios to test: (1) Devil, side B start x=28: at r1 the length-2 dragons head west towards (15,7), not to the (26,0) spawn; (2) a visible pearl 1 step off the path is eaten, one 4 steps off is not; (3) after arriving (head within 3 of the centre) the dragon targets the pile normally and farms the 2x2 fast-tile loops; (4) boundaries: W*H = 1024 (Default 32x32) rushes and W*H = 1056 does not; a centre 25 path steps away does not rush, 24 does; a walled-off centre (DistField FAR) does not; round 30 stops it; (5) Prisoners Dilemma, where the centre is 3 steps from the start and barren: behaviour is almost unchanged; (6) Queen of Spades, a centre 9 steps away with 2 spawn tiles in the central 6x6: the rush ends as soon as the centre is in view. Report centre eats r0-60 and the first-centre-eat round per side, pearls r0-100 and wins on Devil, Trophy, Default Small, Default and Queen of Spades against the swarm rotation, and check that big maps (Big Empty, Schooltime, Stronghold, Trauma) play identical openings.

title: Race for the centre in the opening on small maps: 7003's eliminations are half its losses and start with starters walking the border
hypothesis: Same change as I212 (in flight), with new evidence from submission 7003 (v0030): 14 of its 28 online losses are eliminations, all on maps up to 1024 tiles (Default Small 6, Queen of Spades 3, Devil 2, Prisoners Dilemma 2, Trophy 1). On Default Small the only real spawn is a diagonal strip of gap-25 tiles through the centre (0.77 pearls/round within 6 steps of the centre, 0.32 around the starts; everything else averages a 500-round gap). In 13 of 14 games our two starters walked straight along the border (NNNNNNNNN from (14,11), WWWWWWWWW from (11,14)), ending 10-12 steps from the centre at r12, while the opponents cut diagonally to 0-5 steps in 5 of our 6 losses. Pearl in view in r0-24: us median 43% (22-73) against 42-76%; alive at r50 we had at most half their count in 4 of 6 losses. Devil: in our 3 losses we ate 29-42 pearls in r0-59 against 75-107, with 13% of turns seeing no spawning tile (them 2-5%); in our 5 wins 76-101 against 22-44. After the opening the attrition finishes it: in the 14 eliminations, 171 of the 255 enemy rams that killed us came while we had fewer than 8 dragons, 170 of them while outnumbered, 79 by 2-4-step sprints. Centre richness by map (for I212's bound): the centre beats the starts on Default Small, Devil (5.0 v <=1.05), Trophy (0.78 v <=0.24) and Default (0.27 v <=0.22); it is barren on Stronghold (0.00 v 0.20-0.46), and the starts are richer on Autarky (up to 4.87 v 0.06) and Prisoners Dilemma (up to 10.1 v 1.23), so keep Stronghold out (1152 > 1024) and check Prisoners Dilemma as I212's scenario 5 already does. Report as I212 asks, plus alive at r50 and elimination rate on Default Small, Devil and Queen of Spades.

title: The opening race only from a barren birth view: race.hpp runs for a round-0 dragon only when its first view holds no pearl and no tile known to spawn within P.raceHomeHorizon rounds, on the maps it runs on today
hypothesis: General quantity: our pearls eaten r0-99 and dragons alive at r100 when our start ground is at least as rich as the race's target. E0175 (I294, kept +10.1 over 1554 pairs, now live as submission 8416) sends every round-0 dragon on maps of at most P.raceMaxArea (1024) tiles to where the far mirror lines cross, whatever it sees at home. Its official-map report (runs/E0175/official.json, 100 games against the previous champion, 5 pearl seeds x 2 sides a map) read 43/100: on the 7 official maps where the race fires (Default 1024 tiles, Autarky 972, Queen Of Spades 875, Trophy 625, Devil, Portals and Dilemma 512) it scored 28 of 70 (sign p 0.06 over games; 5 of the 6 maps off level were below 0.5, sign p 0.11), against 15 of 30 on the three maps where it doesn't fire (Trauma, Slithery Fight and Schooltime: identical play, each game the side-mirror of its pair). Default was worst: 2 of 10, 8 lost (sign p 0.055), 3 of them by our elimination (r130, r184, r237). Every one of Default's 1024 tiles spawns pearls, so home is as rich as the middle and the race only spends 10-20 rounds walking; its SPRT agreed (near_default 0.441, n 106, z -2.46; near_portals 0.450, n 106, z -2.07). I462's rebuild of E0175's trials (sprt.json, maps regenerated from their seeds) splits the same way by the true pearl rate within 6 path steps of our starts: under 0.05 a round 0.544 (n 426, z +3.45), 0.5 or more 0.489 (n 329, z -0.87), difference paired z 3.03. An unverified Discord claim points the same way (x_cirno, rank unknown, #general 2026-09-27 07:47 UTC: centralising wins where pearls spawn in the middle, spreading where they spawn at the edges). Change, behind P.raceNeedsBarren: a round-0 dragon races only when its first view (and any team report heard by then) shows no pearl and no countdown due within P.raceHomeHorizon (start 10) rounds; otherwise it plays as the champion before E0175 (targets.hpp's usual pearl and explore choice). Choices its win depends on: scope round-0 dragons on maps up to P.raceMaxArea (children never race, race.hpp's rule); trigger the first view only, decided once, so a race once started runs as today; barren means no pearl and no soon-spawning tile in view, not a rate estimate; left out on purpose: raising the size gate (I462's part) and retuning raceRounds (I463). Expected fire rate: on rich-home small maps every race turn goes (E0175's coder counted the race active on 99 of 424 r0-39 turns a game), on barren-home maps none change; count the changed moves by map style in a shadow copy before the games. Scenarios: (1) Default (every tile spawns): no race, r0-39 moves as v0042's; (2) a near_devil start whose view holds no pearl and no countdown under 10: races as today (near_devil read 0.601 in E0175); (3) boundary: a view whose only countdown is due in P.raceHomeHorizon + 1 rounds races, one due in P.raceHomeHorizon doesn't; (4) a 1152-tile map: unchanged (no race either way). Report the official-map rows for Default, Portals and Autarky and the near_default/near_portals style rows beside the SPRT, and when 8416 has 10+ dev games on Default, its map-matched compare against 8258 there. Siblings: I462 (the same barren gate used to extend the race past P.raceMaxArea; its text leaves small rich-home maps racing, which this changes), I463 (the race's constants). If both this and I462 are kept, the size gate is the part left to delete.

title: Race only along an axis every live symmetry candidate mirrors: while the map's symmetry is unsettled, the opening race keeps the birth coordinate on an axis some live candidate leaves unflipped
hypothesis: General quantity: round-0 dragons whose head stands on middle ground by r20 (tiles whose path distances from the two teams' starts are within a ratio of 0.6), ours against the opponent's. Evidence (devil study 2026-09-28, online games against non-dev teams, every saved game, none kept by result): on Devil since v0042 our round-0 dragons on middle ground by r20 average 0.62 a game against 1.96 for the opponent; when the opponent had more there we scored 5 of 32, otherwise 8 of 16 (rates_p 0.016); the same gap is suggestive on Trophy (3/11 against 20/34, p 0.07) and Schooltime (14/24 against 17/20, p 0.053) and absent on Default, Autarky, Queen Of Spades and Dilemma. Leaders' ranked Devil winners put 2+ round-0 dragons in the middle x 12-19 by r20 in 22 of 25 games, we did in 5 of 48 (p 5e-11), and the side with more heads there at r50 won 22 of 23 decided leader games. Mechanism, from replays and race.hpp: since E0175 (v0043, submission 8416) 93 of our 96 Devil starters step away from the open band y 7-9 (home's only exit) in r1-10, against 17 of 252 before (p 2e-62); they spend 7.6 of r0-10 in the pearl-less home strip against 4.2, only 10 of 96 reach x >= 12 by r20 against 68 of 252 before (p 4e-4) and 50 of 75 for leaders' winners, and 86% end up in the walled lanes x 5-7. race_detail::mirrored counts an axis as mirrored when any live candidate flips it. Devil (SYMMETRY y: a flip of x) cannot rule out the rotation from home, since every tile's rotation image is on the enemy side, so y counts as mirrored and the far line from born y 5, 8 and 11 is the y seam: targets (15,0) and (15,15), the ends of walled 2-wide pockets, instead of (15,5), (15,8) and (15,11) in the middle's gap-30 lane (x 15-16, y 5-10, entered from the open rows 3-4 and 11-12). Unseen edges are assumed open (World::computeStep), so the path runs north or south into home's kelp and up the side lanes before turning back. Trophy (also a flip of x) gets (12,12) with the rotation live against (12,2)/(12,22) without it (not measured here). Change, behind its own switch P.raceAgreedAxes: an axis some live candidate leaves unflipped keeps our birth coordinate (as an unmirrored axis does today) until the candidates agree, then the target is recomputed. Scope: every round-0 dragon while race.hpp runs; the far-line choice, raceKeeps and the size gate stay as they are. Fires: on a single-flip map every round-0 dragon until the rotation is ruled out (6 of 6 a game on Devil, 4 of 4 on Trophy by their start tiles); on a map whose true symmetry is the rotation it fires only while a single-flip candidate is still live, which the measure-first step counts. Measure first, no SPRT games: log (debug line) each round-0 dragon's live candidates and race target at r1, r5 and r10 on 10 devil.map and 10 trophy.map copies (only MAP_NAME changed), 10 each of Default, Queen Of Spades and Dilemma copies, and 20 fresh small maps, both sides, champion and candidate. Round-0 moves before contact barely depend on the opponent, so local games serve for this count. Stop only if, over matched map-sides where the rule changed a target, the candidate's round-0 dragons on middle ground by r20 are fewer than the champion's at chance.sign_p <= 0.1. Report separately how often it fires on rotation-symmetric maps: if single-flip candidates are live at r1 in most of those games, say so and ask the parent before building, since there it switches the race off. Sibling: the next idea (raceKeeps' in-view pearls off the race path); I474 and I462 gate the race on a barren birth view and also change who races on Devil (its birth view holds 600-gap spawn tiles in the x 6-7 lane). Online check once live: Devil and Trophy starters stepping away from the band by r10 and on middle ground by r20, and our score against non-dev teams, matched by opponent and pool period.
